Post-Merger Integration: How International Acquisitions Create Real Value
ERGO Talk International with Theo Kokkalas and Anne Dreller
Theo Kokkalas, Chairman of the Board of ERGO International, and Anne Dreller, Member of the Board of ERGO International
An acquisition can be announced quickly. Whether it becomes a long-term success is decided afterwards. In the latest ERGO Talk International, Theo Kokkalas, Chairman of the Board of ERGO International, and Anne Dreller, Member of the Board of ERGO International, discuss how Post Merger Integration (PMI) determines whether an acquisition translates into sustainable, long-term success.
An Acquisition Is Only the Beginning
International acquisitions have been a key pillar of ERGO’s growth strategy for many years. However, real value is only created when newly acquired companies are successfully integrated into the Group. PMI provides the link between strategic ambition and operational execution. The goal is not to replace local structures, but to combine the strengths of both organisations.

Key Takeaways:
The success of an acquisition is largely determined during the integration phase.
PMI connects strategic growth objectives with sustainable operational results.
Successful integration combines Group-wide standards with local market expertise.
Striking the right balance between harmonisation and entrepreneurial autonomy is a key success factor.
Why Trust Matters More Than Processes
Integration means change, and change creates uncertainty. People naturally wonder what will remain the same, what will change, and whether their corporate culture will be preserved. For Anne Dreller, this is precisely where the most important success factor lies: integrations do not succeed through directives alone, but through transparency, dialogue, and a willingness to develop solutions together.
Successful PMI projects not only preserve local strengths, they also make them accessible to the wider organisation. Step by step, the “Group” and the “market” become one team.
Key Takeaways:
The greatest challenges in integrations are often cultural and organisational rather than technical.
Open and transparent communication builds trust and acceptance.
Successful integration is driven by shared ownership at both Group and local-market level.
Employees benefit from additional expertise, networks, and experience across the ERGO Group.
What Sets Successful Integrations Apart
The experience gained in the Nordics and Baltics demonstrates that successful integration is about far more than harmonising processes. Close collaboration between local markets and Group functions is essential. When different perspectives, experiences, and capabilities come together, they create solutions that individual markets could not develop on their own.
Key Takeaways:
Successful PMI brings together organisations, people, and capabilities across markets.
Local expertise and international perspectives complement one another.
Insights gained from ongoing integrations provide the foundation for future growth initiatives.
Sustainable success is achieved when people, capabilities, and businesses are successfully brought together.
